A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Re3Align, REspGen and REspEval work and contain 29 pages, including Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation experiments with five LLMs across nine settings, alignment-classifier evaluations, robustness analyses and two human studies (Section 6; Appendices A, C and D).

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including generation scores, classifier performance and human-evaluation outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds motivation for the existing retrieval component. Both versions retain BM25 and SPECTER2 retrieval, reciprocal rank fusion, BGE reranking and top-five paragraph selection. Generation, control and refinement procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain EMNLP24 and PeerJ coverage, Re3-Sci/ARIES alignment-training data, and the same author-response generation and evaluation tasks. The new manufacturing-related citation introduces no evaluated domain or scenario.

E2.justification: Phi-4, Qwen3, Llama-3.3, DeepSeek, GPT-4o and the human reference remain in Tables 3 and 12. Table 4 retains the same six alignment classifiers. Shi et al. is background, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The 48-instance generation evaluation, nine experimental settings, metrics, alignment-data splits and human-study procedures remain unchanged. Table 11 retains the same prompts and controls, including the human-response-length-plus-50 limit.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component comparisons, original/rewritten/mismatched-response robustness tests, refinement and discourse analyses, and two richer-input failure case studies (Section 6; Appendices C.2 and D).

E5.justification: Both versions report three evaluation runs, standard deviations and ICC, human agreement and Krippendorff’s alpha, and the same significance-testing and effect-size procedures. Appendix C.2 text moves without changing its statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout, including generation scores in Tables 3, 12 and 14, classifier scores in Table 4, human-study outcomes in Tables 9–10, and the appendix plots and case studies.

T1.justification: Triplet-alignment definitions, metric definitions and the order-fidelity formula remain unchanged. Neither version adds or removes mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning author input, controllability, evaluation and refinement. The added appendix citation does not redefine the paper’s core claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of input specificity, control–quality trade-offs and refinement, together with the stated limitations, are unchanged. Appendix B.2’s added general grounding motivation reiterates the existing rationale without introducing a substantive new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Retrieval specifications, alignment thresholds, prompts, hardware information and code/data access disclosures are retained. The added Appendix B.2 introduction supplies no new implementation detail or reproducibility instruction.

R1.justification: v3 adds Shi et al. (2026), concerning cognitive digital twins for manufacturing, to the references and cites it in Appendix B.2 as motivation for retrieval-augmented generation. Other citations and the broader research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix B.2 expands its opening purpose statement into a short literature-based motivation for retrieval. The main text, section sequence and remaining appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: The additions cause reference and appendix text reflow. Table 8 moves from the left to the right column on page 17, and Appendix D begins on page 19 instead of page 18. Figures and table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds limited attribution and background for an already explained retrieval component in Appendix B.2. The scientific argument, experimental support, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged. The accompanying layout shifts provide no material improvement or deterioration in readability.
